The problem was that the lead French agency wasn’t an air accident investigation authority, as would have been the case had the accident happened in the UK, or pretty much anywhere else

The two accident investigation authorities were France’s Bureau d’Enquêtes et d’Analyses and the UK’s Air Accidents Investigation Branch – with the AAIB providing support to the BEA as the lead investigative authority
But, unlike investigations in most other countries, the BEA and the AAIB were subordinate to the Gonesse préfet (prefect) and his team, which took some getting used to
This was a criminal investigation as well as an air accident investigation, we were told, and the criminal investigation took priority
